content.thinking: I need to fix the wording of CF-2 and leave the rest as it is.

action_items.item: Roll out feature flag switch-ons in production to a small share of traffic first, and widen them only while the service's error rate stays at its usual level.
Require tests that exercise the code path a feature flag turns on, including shoppers with no purchases in the period it covers, before that flag can be switched on in production.
Decide whether `average_spend_per_item`, used with the flag off, should still raise for an account with no purchases at all, which the current tests expect. If it should not, fix it.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the account page error rate rose far above its usual level.

The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError: division by zero in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, at the line the log names. This error started in the minute the flag was switched on and kept going until the log lines that were read end.

ruled_out.what: A deploy or release. The production change events that were read returned no deploy, only the flag change.
Another flag change. The flag provider's history showed no other flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour before it was read.

causal_chain.step: The account page reached that code because admin switched on the feature flag monthly-spend-feature at {P1.1}. The page's flag evaluations were all off over {G7e5d.4}, split between off and on in {G971b.6}, and all on over {Gce95.4}.

With the flag on, the account page's figure is computed by dividing the month's spend by the number of purchases made this month, and that number is zero for a shopper who has bought before but not this month.

input.cause_in_plain_words: An administrator switched on a new feature for the account page, and it likely sent shoppers who had bought nothing this month through a calculation that divides by their number of purchases this month, which fails when that number is zero.

contributing_factors.factor: When monthly-spend-feature was switched on, it reached the account page's whole traffic within the minute after the change. No staged rollout, or check of the error rate on a small share of traffic, was seen before that.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A staged rollout would have shown the division error on a small share of account page requests and stopped there, so far fewer shoppers would have had failed pages.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No test was seen that exercises the account page with monthly-spend-feature on for a shopper who has no purchases this month. By Code-Fix's reading, the existing tests in the files it read expect the flag-off path's error for an account with no purchases at all.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division error would have been caught before the flag was switched on in production.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent formed candidate C1, which tied the failures to the monthly-spend-feature flag change and the division error in the logs.
The Mitigation Agent reverted monthly-spend-feature from on to off. This needed no deploy and can be put back.
The Mitigation Agent confirmed that the service had left the incident's level after the revert.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request for a person to review.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, the account page's spend summary goes through `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the month's total by the number of purchases marked as this month's, and has no case for a shopper who has bought before but not this month: for that shopper the count is zero and the division raises ZeroDivisionError.
input.still_at_risk: Switching monthly-spend-feature back on before a fix is in place could again fail account pages for shoppers with no purchases this month, and by Code-Fix's reading, the account page can still fail with the flag off for an account with no purchases at all.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for many shoppers
